segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: Listen to a talk in an art history class.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: If you've ever looked at a Picasso painting and thought, wait, is that a face or a guitar?

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: You've already encountered the magic of Cubism.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: This revolutionary movement shook up the art scene in the early 20th century.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: It wasn't just a new style.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: It was a complete reimagining of how we see and represent reality.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: Artists like Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque broke away from the traditional rules of perspective and instead chose to depict objects from multiple angles at once.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: Imagine seeing every side of a coffee cup, top, bottom and side, all in a single image.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: How this coffee cup is depicted, that's the kind of visual remix Cubism brought to the canvas.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: At first, people didn't know what to make of it.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: Critics called it chaotic, even nonsensical.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: But over time, Cubism proved to be a game changer, influencing not just painting and sculpture, but also music, literature, and architecture.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: It encouraged creators to rethink structure, narrative, and form, and to reconsider how we think about representation and abstraction.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: And it paved the way for other art movements, like modernism.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: Modernism also embraced abstraction and conceptual depth, though in somewhat different ways.
